software.p1: In most companies someone spends part of every day copying things from one place to another: webshop orders into the invoicing system, enquiries from the contact form into a spreadsheet, the spreadsheet into the monthly report. It isn't a mistake, just expensive — and it's the first thing to slip when things get busy.

software.p3: We start with an assessment: you get a written summary of which processes are worth automating and which aren't. Every automation logs its runs and raises an alert on failure, because a process that stops silently is worse than doing it by hand.

Each month we record what the site actually loads, and a web lawyer reviews the change. Compliance is their call, not ours.

faq.question: Do you guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. Compliance is a legal determination and a lawyer makes it. What we guarantee: the technical barriers get assessed, documented and removed, and you get a written record of what changed.

faq.question: Does Pulse fix problems automatically?
faq.answer: No. Pulse detects and reports. Fixing is either a separate instruction or comes out of a monthly retainer — because an automatic change to a live site without anyone looking at it is how outages happen.

faq.question: Does the Pulse legal module guarantee compliance?
faq.answer: No. A lawyer determines compliance, not us. What the module gives you: a monthly record of which cookies and third-party scripts the site actually loads, and when that drifts from the legal documents, a web lawyer reviews and updates them as needed. The lawyer sets the scope and fee of the legal work.

faq.question: How is the final price set?
faq.answer: After scoping. We discuss what you need, review the existing systems, then give a fixed price and date — not a range.

faq.question: Can you work white-label?
faq.answer: Yes, and most of our agency work is. Your client relationship stays yours. If you'd rather name us, that's fine too.

faq.question: Does a small office need outside IT support?
faq.answer: Often it's the small ones that need it most. Without an in-house IT person, someone usually handles it on the side, and that works until something breaks. We start with an assessment and tell you how much ongoing work your setup actually needs. If it's not much, we say so.

faq.question: Do we have to replace our existing systems to automate?
faq.answer: Usually not. We connect what you already have: the webshop, the invoicing system, the spreadsheets. We only recommend new software when the existing one can't do what's needed — and the assessment explains why in writing.

faq.question: What happens if an automation stops?
faq.answer: It doesn't stop silently. Every run is logged, and a failure sends an alert to whoever is responsible — us, if you hand over operations, or the person you designate. Missed items can be processed again from the log.

Seo.intro: Search has split in two. Google measures the technical foundation; AI search reads structured data, not marketing prose. We build both — and we don't just talk about it.

proofPanel.claim: Robots.txt — sitemap and AI crawlers by name

Seo.proofClosing: Most SEO agencies don't have a sitemap on their own site. Go and look — seriously, open it. If any of ours doesn't work, tell us and we'll fix it.
Seo.changedLeftBody: Load speed, layout stability and response time are ranking factors now, not comfort issues. A slow site doesn't lose because it's ugly — it loses because Google ranks it lower.
Seo.changedRightBody: More people simply ask an AI. These systems don't read keywords, they read structure. If that structure isn't machine-readable, someone else appears in the answer.

Seo.aiTestTitle: We ask the machine, more than once
Seo.aiTestBody: Together we put together the questions your buyers would actually ask an AI. Then we ask them, and write down what came back.

aiTestFacts.label: Platforms
aiTestFacts.text: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot and Claude, plus Google's AI Overview where it appears.

aiTestFacts.label: Repetition
aiTestFacts.text: At least three runs per question, each in a fresh session with no history, on desktop and on mobile. AI answers change from run to run; a single test proves nothing.

aiTestFacts.label: Delivery
aiTestFacts.text: Every answer verbatim, with date and platform, plus a summary: how often you were mentioned, and whether what you do was described accurately.

Seo.aiTestNote: This is a snapshot, not a guarantee: nobody can promise an AI will recommend you. If we do the fixes with you, we re-run the same question set so you can see what changed.

processSteps.title: 01 · Assessment
processSteps.body: Where you stand: speed, indexing, structure, structured data. You get a list of what's missing — whether or not you continue with us.

processSteps.title: 02 · Build
processSteps.body: Fixing the technical foundation. If the current system can't carry it, a rebuild — but phased, so you don't lose traffic on the way.

processSteps.title: 03 · Maintenance
processSteps.body: Search engines change, and so does your site. If you want operations too, we track it.

faq.question: How long before results show?
faq.answer: Technical fixes appear in indexing within weeks. Ranking movement is slower — three to six months for competitive terms. Anyone promising faster either doesn't understand it or isn't being honest.

faq.question: Do you guarantee first position?
faq.answer: No, and avoid anyone who does. Google decides ranking, not your supplier. What we can guarantee: the technical foundation will be sound, measurable, and verifiable by you.

faq.question: Is AEO actually worth it?
faq.answer: It brings little traffic today, but it's growing fast — and the structured data it requires also helps in conventional Google results. So it isn't wasted spend even if AI search grows slower than expected.

faq.question: What's the difference between SEO and AEO?
faq.answer: SEO aims to move you up Google's results. AEO aims to make sure that when someone asks an AI assistant, it can talk about you accurately and cite you as a source. The foundations largely overlap: a fast, clean site that makes sense as text. AEO adds structured data and content organised as questions and answers.

faq.question: Can AEO be measured?
faq.answer: Not the way Google rankings can: there's no public ranking, and AI answers vary from run to run. That's why we ask several times on several platforms, and why we hand over the answers verbatim. Your analytics will also show visitors arriving from AI platforms such as chatgpt.com or perplexity.ai.

faq.question: How long does the AEO assessment take?
faq.answer: 72 hours from when the question set is agreed. In that time you get, in writing, what a search engine and an AI assistant see of your site, what the AIs answered to your questions, and what's worth fixing.

faq.question: What do you need from me?
faq.answer: Facts. What you offer, to whom, since when, which partner statuses and references you have, and what buyers ask you. The content is built from those: we don't make up claims about your company.

faq.question: Can you improve an existing site, or only build new?
faq.answer: Both. The assessment tells you which is better value — sometimes fixing the current system is cheaper and faster.

faq.question: How do I know you actually did it?
faq.answer: The same way you can check us: sitemap, robots.txt, Rich Results Test, PageSpeed. Public, free tools — you don't have to take our word for it.

About.headline: We didn't start as developers.
About.intro1: Two decades in sales and marketing came before a line of code. Which is why the question here isn't which technology to build with — it's whether it brings customers.
About.intro2: The company is six years old. The experience behind it is older.

timeline.label: Sales
timeline.heading: Started in direct sales
timeline.body: That's where the important lesson came from: the buyer doesn't care about the product, only whether it solves their problem. Every decision since has followed from that.

timeline.label: Digital
timeline.heading: The market moved online
timeline.body: Commercial experience combined with campaign management and pages built to convert. From then on it was measurable which worked and which didn't.

timeline.label: The company
timeline.heading: GBR Marketing Solutions Kft. was founded
timeline.body: Not as an agency, but to turn what had been one person's work into a system.

timeline.label: Build and operate
timeline.heading: Today we don't just advertise
timeline.body: We build the system underneath. We develop and operate our own products too — not for the portfolio, but because that's how you learn what being responsible for a live system means.

About.howWeWorkIntro: We're not a large agency and we don't intend to become one. Most of the work happens in-house, where we can answer for the quality directly. Where specialist skill is needed, we bring in partners we've worked with before.

About.declineBody: There are things we don't do — and we say so upfront. You're better off being sent to someone who does it well than having us start and discover halfway that we can't.
About.alsoLine: We also work as a development partner for Hungarian and Western European agencies alike.

principles.title: 01 · We tell you when something isn't working
principles.body: If a campaign isn't producing, we report it rather than dress it up. If a project is slipping, you hear it in advance, not on the deadline. Bad news on time is worth more than good news late.

principles.title: 02 · We don't promise what we can't measure
principles.body: Rankings, returns, customer numbers — we don't guarantee those, because we don't determine them. What we do guarantee: technical quality, the deadline, and that you can verify what was built.

principles.title: 03 · We don't take every project
principles.body: If a project isn't a fit, we say so at the start, not halfway through. That's why we ask first, and why there's a budget question on the form.
